item.title: The Best College Gymnastics Team from the Past 10 Years
item.dc:creator: Halle Winfrey
item.description:
College gymnastics, for NCAA Divisions I, II, and III, has four different categories that the gymnasts perform in to get their overall score. The teams are ranked by the total of the four events, which can be scored out of 200.00.  Gymnasts are scored in vault, uneven bars, balance beam and floor exercise. A perfect score in any of these categories is a 10.0, and every gymnast wants to reach that perfect score. For a vault routine, the gymnast is scored on just one, single vault. The uneven bars routine consists of two different height bars, where the gymnast flips from one to the other during their routine. The balance beam is a routine that can last up to 90 seconds that consists of different flips and turns. Lastly, the floor exercise is a choreographed routine where the gymnasts can show off their skills to music. 

There has been some consistencies over the years with the top teams, some teams even win back-to-back years, multiple years in a row. But, who has had the highest overall scores from the past 10 years? Who is “the best?” Also, who is the best out of the Big Ten teams? Which Big Ten team has consistently had the highest scores? 

That’s our mission today; figuring out who the best of the best is. 

In order to find this out, there are some steps that needed to be taken in order to get this started. First, I took each team’s overall score from the past 10 years and filtered out any score that was lower than 196; just to be able to get a more accurate chart. Also to get the most accurate chart, I am using each teams’ high score from the data. 

Now to get the results.

Code 
library(tidyverse)
library(ggbump)
library(ggrepel)
library(gt)

totals <- read_csv("womens_gymnastics_aa_rankings_last10seasons.csv")

big10 <- totals |> filter(con == "Big Ten") 
goodprograms <- totals |> filter(high > 196)
ok <- totals |> filter(name == "Oklahoma") 
fl <- totals |> filter(name == "Florida")
lsu <- totals |> filter(name == "LSU")

ggplot() + 
  geom_bump(data=goodprograms, aes(x=season, y=high, group=name), color="grey") +
  geom_point(data=goodprograms, aes(x=season, y=high,), size = 4, color="grey") + 
  geom_bump(data=ok, aes(x=season, y=high, group=name), color="red") +
  geom_point(data=ok, aes(x=season, y=high, group=name), size = 4, color="red") +
  geom_bump(data=fl, aes(x=season, y=high, group=name), color="orange") +
  geom_point(data=fl, aes(x=season, y=high, group=name), size = 4, color="orange") +
  geom_bump(data=lsu, aes(x=season, y=high, group=name), color="purple") +
  geom_point(data=lsu, aes(x=season, y=high, group=name), size = 4, color="purple") +
  geom_text(data=ok |> filter(season == max(season)), aes(x=season + .7, y=high+.3, group=name, label=name)) + 
  geom_text(data=ok |> filter(season == min(season)), aes(x=season - .7, y=high, group=name, label=name)) + 
  geom_text(data=fl |> filter(season == max(season)), aes(x=season + .7, y=high, group=name, label=name)) + 
  geom_text(data=fl |> filter(season == min(season)), aes(x=season - .7, y=high, group=name, label=name)) + 
  geom_text(data=lsu |> filter(season == max(season)), aes(x=season + .7, y=high, group=name, label=name)) + 
  geom_text(data=lsu |> filter(season == min(season)), aes(x=season - .7, y=high, group=name, label=name)) +
  scale_x_continuous(limits=c(2016,2027), breaks = c(2017, 2019, 2021, 2023, 2025))  +
  labs(
    x="The Season", 
    y="Highest Score from the Season", 
    title="Which Gymnastics Team Has the Best 
    Overall Score?", 
    subtitle="Using all data from the past 10 years in order to find who is the best college team overall.", 
    caption="Source: Road to Nationals | By Halle Winfrey"
    ) +
  theme_minimal() + 
  theme(
    plot.title = element_text(size = 20, face = "bold"),
    axis.title = element_text(size = 8), 
    plot.subtitle = element_text(size=10), 
    panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
    plot.title.position = "plot"
    )

All of the teams have really close scores, since the judges use decimals and exact numbers in order to score each team. 

But from the chart, we can see the top three college teams from the past 10 years are Oklahoma, LSU and Florida. If we want to be really specific, the top three teams are actually Oklahoma’s 2024, 2023 and 2026 teams. Then it’s Florida’s 2023 team, then Oklahoma’s 2020 team, lastly LSU’s 2024 team. Oklahoma has had some of the highest scores out of all of the teams from the past 10 years. 

Next, I wanted to figure out from all of the best teams, who in the Big Ten is the best? We know Oklahoma is the best overall, but I wanted to filter out all of the other teams and focus on the Big Ten. 

So I did just that. 

I started out by taking all of the overall scores and creating a filter to make it just the Big Ten. When I found the top three teams, I created a line chart in order to be able to visualize just how close the teams really are. Again, I used each team’s high score and compared them to each other.

Code 
mi <- big10 |> filter(name == "Michigan")
cal <- big10 |> filter(name == "UCLA")
min <- big10 |> filter(name == "Minnesota")

ggplot() +
  geom_line(data=big10, aes(x=season, y=high, group=name), color="grey") +
  geom_line(data=mi, aes(x=season, y=high), color="darkgreen") + 
  geom_line(data=cal, aes(x=season, y=high), color="gold") +
  geom_line(data=min, aes(x=season, y=high), color="darkred") +
  geom_text(data=mi |> filter(season == max(season)), aes(x=season + .7, y=high-.1, group=name, label=name)) + 
  geom_text(data=mi |> filter(season == min(season)), aes(x=season - .7, y=high, group=name, label=name)) + 
  geom_text(data=cal |> filter(season == max(season)), aes(x=season + .7, y=high, group=name, label=name)) + 
  geom_text(data=cal |> filter(season == min(season)), aes(x=season - .7, y=high, group=name, label=name)) + 
  geom_text(data=min |> filter(season == max(season)), aes(x=season + .7, y=high, group=name, label=name)) + 
  geom_text(data=min |> filter(season == min(season)), aes(x=season - .7, y=high, group=name, label=name)) +
  scale_x_continuous(limits=c(2015,2027), breaks = c(2017, 2019, 2021, 2023, 2025)) +
  labs(
    x="The Season", 
    y="Highest Score from the Season", 
    title="The Best of the Best", 
    subtitle="Out of all of the high scores, who in the Big Ten has the best overall score from the past 10 years?", 
    caption="Source: Road to Nationals | By Halle Winfrey"
    ) +
  theme_minimal() + 
  theme(
    plot.title = element_text(size = 20, face = "bold"),
    axis.title = element_text(size = 8), 
    plot.subtitle = element_text(size=10), 
    panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
    plot.title.position = "plot"
    )

The #1 Big Ten team is the Michigan team from the 2022 season; then Michigan again with their 2023 season. Then it goes to UCLA’s 2026 team; then Michigan again with their 2024 team. Then, UCLA again with their 2025 team; then Michigan again with their 2024 season. Then the trend ends with Minnesota’s 2022 season. 

Again, there are a lot of consistencies with the best teams, but there are some other teams that are able to get recognition as well. 

Then, after figuring out the best teams from their overall score, I wanted to figure out from all of the Big Ten teams, which one is the best at Floor Exercise routines, again from the past 10 years. 

To start, I took all of the floor exercise data from each team and filtered out all of the non-Big Ten teams. Then also filtered out any score lower than 48; again because the scores are really close and there are a lot of them. After finding the top three teams, I created a table comparing each team’s high score and their average scores.

Code 
fx <- read_csv("womens_gymnastics_fx_rankings_last10seasons.csv")

big <- fx |> filter(con == "Big Ten")
best <- big |> filter(ave > 48) |> filter(rqs > 0)

ave <- best |> 
  group_by(name) |> 
  summarise(
    average = mean(ave),
    high = mean(high))

bigave <- ave |> 
  pivot_longer(
    cols=-name, 
    names_to="type", 
    values_to="average")

ave |>
  gt() |>
  cols_label(
    name = "College Team",
    average = "Average Score",
    high = "High Score"
  ) |>
  tab_header(
    title = "The Big Ten's Floor Exercise",
    subtitle = "The Big Ten Conference teams are close in scoring for floor exercises, but who has the highest score?"
  ) |> tab_style(
    style = cell_text(color = "black", weight = "bold", align = "left"),
    locations = cells_title("title")
  ) |> tab_style(
    style = cell_text(color = "black", align = "left"),
    locations = cells_title("subtitle")
  ) |>
  tab_source_note(
    source_note = md("By: Halle Winfrey | Source: Road to Nationals")
  ) |>
  tab_style(
     locations = cells_column_labels(columns = everything()),
     style = list(
       cell_borders(sides = "bottom", weight = px(3)),
       cell_text(weight = "bold", size=12)
     )
   ) |>
  opt_row_striping() |> 
  opt_table_lines("none") |> 
   data_color(
    columns = vars(average),
    colors = scales::col_numeric(
      palette = c(
        "white", "orange", "red"),
      domain = NULL)
  ) |> 
   data_color(
    columns = vars(high),
    colors = scales::col_numeric(
      palette = c(
        "white", "orange", "red"),
      domain = NULL)
  )
The Big Ten's Floor Exercise
The Big Ten Conference teams are close in scoring for floor exercises, but who has the highest score?

Maryland 49.02510 49.39000
Michigan 49.33190 49.59250
Michigan State 49.14800 49.51944
Minnesota 49.25300 49.57250
Nebraska 49.04820 49.40750

Penn State 48.96190 49.34250
Rutgers 48.80280 49.26750
UCLA 49.47500 49.75000

By: Halle Winfrey | Source: Road to Nationals

When it comes to floor exercise, the highest score goes to Iowa with 49.45000. Then it’s Illinois with a high score of 49.38571. The third place spot goes to Illinois-Champaign with a high score of 49.35000. 

Like we have established, there are a lot of back-to-back winning seasons for some teams; like we saw with Oklahoma. But, each category is different, and each team’s specialty category is different.
